name: Receive
purpose: Establish the ticket as a tracked unit of work with a defensible timestamp.

prompts.label: Acknowledged receipt to the reporter?
prompts.help: This sets expectations and starts the clock.

prompts.label: Reporter identity and channel
prompts.help: Who reported it, and through what channel.

prompts.label: Perceived onset, if different from the report
prompts.help: When the reporter believes the problem actually started.

prompts.label: Environment
prompts.help: Production, staging, a specific tenant, a specific region.

prompts.label: Attached evidence
prompts.help: Screenshots, log excerpts, links, anything the reporter provided.

prompts.label: What was NOT provided
prompts.help: That absence is your first set of clarifying questions.

mindset: What is the minimum I need to know before I can decide how urgent this is?
Who else needs to know that this ticket exists?
antiPatterns: Jumping to a fix before understanding the symptom.
Marking as resolved because the reporter went quiet. The issue may still be live.
Assuming the reported symptom is the actual problem. Reporters describe what they see, not what is broken.
output: Ticket with metadata and provisional priority

name: Parse the reported symptom
purpose: Separate the symptom the reporter observed from the hypothesis they formed from the defect that actually exists.

prompts.label: Restate the problem in your own words
prompts.help: This surfaces misunderstandings early and costs nothing.

prompts.label: Observable facts
prompts.help: What the user did, what they expected, what happened instead, when it started, whether it is still happening, whether it reproduces consistently.

prompts.label: The reporter's diagnosis (set aside)
prompts.help: Record the theory, but treat it as a hypothesis to test rather than a fact to build on.

prompts.label: Scope
prompts.help: One user or many, one feature or several, one environment or all, one region or global.

prompts.label: Clarifying questions asked
prompts.help: Specific and closed-ended: does this happen in incognito mode, does it happen on another device, what time did you first notice, what is the exact error text.

mindset: Is this a symptom I have seen before, or is it novel?
What would have to be true for this report to be accurate?

name: Classify
purpose: Assign a category — what kind of problem — and a severity — how urgent. These two axes drive everything downstream.

prompts.label: Category
prompts.help: Assigned from the taxonomy, based on Phase 1 evidence.

prompts.label: Provisional severity
prompts.help: By impact: how many users, how critical the function, whether a workaround exists, whether data is at risk, whether a deadline or regulatory obligation applies.

prompts.label: Severity reconsidered?
prompts.help: The most common assessment error is under-classifying an early ticket that later proves severe.

prompts.label: Duplicate of an existing ticket?
prompts.help: If this is the same issue as another open ticket, link them.

prompts.label: Checked against a security lens?
prompts.help: Every unknown ticket deserves a check for a security issue in disguise.

mindset: If I were the customer, how bad would this be?
What is the worst-case interpretation of this report?
Is there any way this is a security issue in disguise?
antiPatterns: Inflating severity to get attention. It erodes trust in the whole scale.
Deflating severity because the reporter is junior or the symptom seems trivial.
Skipping the security question. Every unknown ticket deserves a check against a security lens.

name: Contextualize
purpose: Enrich the ticket with everything the system already knows about itself, so the assessment rests on evidence rather than speculation.

prompts.label: Recent changes
prompts.help: Deploys, config changes and infrastructure changes in the last 24 to 72 hours; feature flag toggles, schema migrations, credential rotations; third-party incidents reported by vendors.

prompts.label: Service health
prompts.help: Dashboards for the affected service, SLO burn rate, error rate, latency, saturation, dependency health. Is this isolated, or the leading edge of a trend?

prompts.label: Error tracker
prompts.help: Is the reported error already captured, at what frequency, on which release, with what stack trace?

prompts.label: Logs and traces
prompts.help: Search by user ID, transaction ID or timestamp, and look for correlated errors in a window around the report.

prompts.label: RUM and session replay
prompts.help: Where the report is user-facing: what did the user actually see, and what did they actually do?

prompts.label: Patterns
prompts.help: Are others reporting similar symptoms, is this a known recurrence, is this the first of a wave?

prompts.label: Evidence bundle
prompts.help: Relevant deploys, dashboard snapshots, error tracker links, log excerpts, and replay links, gathered in one place. This is what supports the Phase 4 decision, and what gets handed over if the ticket is escalated.

mindset: What changed recently? Most incidents correlate with a change.
What does the system say about itself, independent of what the reporter said?
What would I see if this were systemic rather than a one-off?

name: Triage and decide
purpose: Commit to a path: resolve at the desk, escalate to a team, declare an incident, or request more information.

prompts.label: Named decision

options.label: Investigate — this becomes a work ticket
Request specific information and pause the ticket

prompts.help: Decision tree: Is impact severe or growing? Is the cause known with a runbook? Is the issue within my team's ownership? Is it clearly owned by another team? Is the report ambiguous?

prompts.label: Reasoning
prompts.help: Name the decision out loud — "I am declaring an incident" is a decision.

prompts.label: What evidence would change my mind?
prompts.help: If nothing would, you have stopped assessing.

mindset: What is the cost of being wrong in each direction? A delayed incident is worse than a false alarm; a needless page is worse than a ticket.
What is the specific decision I am making right now?
What evidence would change my mind?

name: Act
purpose: Execute the chosen path, with discipline.

prompts.label: Path taken
prompts.help: Determined by the Phase 4 decision.

prompts.label: Actions taken
prompts.help: Execute steps in order, checking expected output after each. If output deviates, stop and reassess. Do not improvise under pressure.

prompts.label: Deviations from runbook or expectation
prompts.help: Note any deviation for later improvement.

prompts.label: Outcome
prompts.help: Confirm resolution against the original symptom, not merely the runbook's success criterion.

mindset: Am I making the system better, or just making the symptom go away?
What would I want to know if I were the person taking over from me?
Is the clock still running, and does the customer know what is happening?

name: Record and close
purpose: Close the loop: update the ticket, update the knowledge base, and where warranted trigger the post-incident process.

prompts.label: Ticket updated with resolution, cause, evidence, time, follow-ups?
Post-mortem needed?
prompts.help: Always for SEV1 and SEV2; likely for a SEV3 with an unusual cause; not for a known issue resolved by runbook.

prompts.label: Runbook amended or added?
prompts.help: Amend if it was incomplete; add one if the issue was novel and will recur.

prompts.label: Alert added?
prompts.help: Add if detection was slow.

prompts.label: Test added?
prompts.help: Add if the defect should have been caught earlier.

prompts.label: Learning broadcast to other teams?
prompts.help: Where the issue is likely to recur or affects other teams.

prompts.label: What would the next responder need that they did not have this time?
Which phase changed the outcome?
prompts.help: This is the column that turns a case log into a portfolio artifact.

mindset: What would the next responder need that they did not have this time?
Did this ticket produce any change to the system, or only a resolution?
Would I recognize this same issue faster next time?
output: Updated ticket, runbook, alerts, tests, post-mortem
